stem: Which of the following pancreatic islet cell types produces insulin?

options.label: A
options.text: Alpha cells of the pancreatic islets
options.misconception: Glucagon-secreting alpha cells are being confused with insulin-secreting beta cells.
options.explanation: Alpha cells produce glucagon in response to low blood glucose; they do not produce insulin.

options.label: B
options.text: Beta cells of the pancreatic islets
options.misconception: None; beta cells are the insulin-producing islet cells.
options.explanation: Beta cells produce insulin and make up approximately 75 percent of each pancreatic islet.

options.label: C
options.text: Delta cells of the pancreatic islets
options.misconception: Somatostatin-secreting delta cells are being confused with beta cells.
options.explanation: Delta cells secrete somatostatin, which inhibits insulin and glucagon release; they do not produce insulin.

options.label: D
options.text: PP cells of the pancreatic islets
options.misconception: Pancreatic polypeptide cells are being confused with insulin-producing cells.
options.explanation: PP cells secrete pancreatic polypeptide and are not the source of insulin.

options.label: E
options.text: Acinar cells of the exocrine pancreas
options.misconception: Exocrine digestive enzyme cells are being confused with endocrine islet cells.
options.explanation: Acinar cells secrete digestive enzymes into the pancreatic duct; insulin comes from islet beta cells.

context: Learning objective: identify the insulin-producing islet cell. Pancreatic islets contain alpha (glucagon), beta (insulin), delta (somatostatin), and PP cells; beta cells are the insulin source (~75% of each islet).
